answer: An agent economy can assign paid work through a public randomness beacon: the beacon draws one qualified agent per job from the atlas of registered identities, so a Sybil farmer cannot steer every job to its own clones. Each drawn agent posts a small bond and must deliver by a deadline, with delivery checked against the task's trellis of acceptance tests. Failed or copied work burns the bond and strikes the identity; three strikes prune it from the atlas. A thousand clones means a thousand bonds at risk with no guarantee of being chosen, while one honest agent simply waits for its fair draw.
